findings.summary: Main Registry references paragraph still out of sync with the code and the new callout: it says GuardedAccess 'reserves 16 slots first' (now a per-body count, 2 for method lookup/HasMethod/nil-ing), says 'No path of the engine can do that now' and 'What is still not protected is what the paragraph above lists', while the callout (line ~164) now lists binding references (require, make_object in GetComponent/AddComponent, Subscribe/AddOnClick arguments) that can still terminate on web/MSVC Debug; the duplicated ReleaseScript sentence from the previous review is still there.
findings.scenario: A reader of the main paragraph concludes no engine path can std::terminate at the cap on the web build and that every guarded body reserves 16 slots; both are contradicted by the callout and by LuaComponent.cpp (GuardedAccess(..., 2)).

findings.summary: AMetamethodThatRetiresTheInstanceWhileTheFieldsAreListedIsSurvived does not pin the regression it targets: EXPECT_FALSE(fields.empty()) is always true (DescribeFields always adds the scriptUUID field), and the old nullptr crash is only reached if Lua's lua_next visits 'a' before 'b', which is unspecified hash order.
findings.scenario: On a build where 'b' is visited before 'a', the old code (lua_gettop(_scriptInstance.lua_state()) after the retire) would also pass this test, because no definition is read after the retire; a future regression of the valid() check would go unnoticed. Asserting the field names, or adding more definitions after the retiring one, would make it deterministic.
